subject: Purchase-order variance request — Merchantly pilot
messages:
From: Jules Park <procurement@merchantly.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Purchase-order variance request for pilot engagement

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We’re excited to move the Merchantly pilot forward. Before we can kick off, our procurement team asked whether Redwood can accept an invoice-only payment path for the initial 30-day pilot instead of issuing a purchase order.

Summary:
- Pilot value: $9,500 (one month)
- Merchantly legal: standard MSAs signed in-clause, SOW attached
- Reason: Merchantly’s AP system is in a scheduled migration; they cannot raise POs until Dec 1

Attached: Merchantly_SOW.pdf, W9_Merchantly.pdf, PO-variance-form.pdf (we filled our internal variance form).

Can Redwood accommodate a temporary no-PO route with the following safeguards?
1) Invoice routed to accounting with a single-payment approval limit of $10k
2) Merchantly signs attestation that PO will be provided after Dec 1
3) Redwood procurement retains right to pause services if PO is not provided within 45 days

Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Jules Park
Vendor Ops | Merchantly Inc

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jules Park <procurement@merchantly.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Purchase-order variance request for pilot engagement

Marissa / Priya — forwarding Merchantly’s ask (thread below). They’re a 30-day pilot, under $10k, and have provided SOW + W9.

Marissa: commercial OK on our side? Does this align with the pilot terms we approved with Sales?
Priya: procurement / finance — can we approve a temporary invoice-only path with the safeguards Jules proposed? If not, what conditions do we need (evidence, countersignature, GL code, PO holdback)?

If we can’t make an exception, let me know and I’ll ask Merchantly for a purchase-order ETA. Would like to keep momentum.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Purchase-order variance request for pilot engagement

Thanks for the ping. Quick read: pilot size and docs look reasonable but procurement needs a short paper trail and mitigate risk. We can provisionally approve a 45-day invoice-only intake under these conditions: 

1) Merchantly completes the PO-variance-form.pdf (they attached a draft; we need it countersigned by Merchantly and an internal Merchantly approver)
2) Merchantly provides a target date by which they will issue a PO (we require PO by 2026-12-01)
3) Redwood Sales owner (Marissa) must confirm commercial acceptance and append a one-line memo to the invoice indicating "pilot — invoice-only variance approved"
4) Finance will place a temporary hold: services activated, invoiced to AP, but payment release will require one finance-level approval and verification of GL code CHA-TRIALS-01
5) Procurement will require Merchantly to agree to a 2% holdback clause that is released when PO is provided (covers the case of non-delivery of PO).

If Merchantly accepts, I’ll prepare a short waiver memo for internal approvals and route to Accounting for a one-time payment release. I’ve attached our standard procurement-checklist (procurement-checklist.xlsx).

Priya Natarajan
Sr. Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: procurement-checklist.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jules Park <procurement@merchantly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Purchase-order variance request for pilot engagement

Jules — thanks, and appreciate the fast turnaround. We can agree to the provisional invoice-only path with the conditions Priya outlined. Please: 

1) Review and countersign the attached PO-variance-form.pdf (I included highlighted fields for the Merchantly approver)
2) Confirm a PO issuance target date (you indicated Dec 1 in your note; please confirm)
3) Send final invoice referencing DEAL-8892 and GL code CHA-TRIALS-01 once services begin

We’ll execute the internal waiver memo and release payment once Accounting confirms the invoice and approvals. If Merchantly cannot provide the signed variance form today, we can sign a short DocuSign waiver — let us know preference.

Looking forward to getting the pilot live.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: PO-variance-form.pdf
